newsitem.title: FRANCE: ALPINE SKIING-GERG AND SEIZINGER SCORE GERMAN ONE-TWO.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-GERG AND SEIZINGER SCORE GERMAN ONE-TWO.

text.p: Hilde Gerg, the girl wonder of German Alpine skiing, beat compatriot Katja Seizinger to give their country a superb double in a World Cup super-G race on Thursday.

Gerg, one of the most promising skiers on the women's circuit since she won her first World Cup victory in a super-G in 1994 in Sierra Nevada, was the only starter to finish under the 1:08 barrier on the OK piste.
The 21-year-old from Lenggries clocked 1:07.81, with Seizinger second on 1:08.20 and world champion Isolde Kostner of Italy third, 0.18 seconds behind the current overall World Cup leader.
The outcome was hardly a surprise as Gerg had already taken third place in one of two super-G's won by Seizinger in the French resort last year. Kostner had also taken second place in one of them.
If the podium looked familiar, the weather was unusually sunny for a mid-December in Savoy, making the course faster and favouring real specialists.

"I did not find it difficult. I did not have the impression I was skiing that fast," said Gerg, who was second to Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg in the opening super-G of the season in Lake Louise, Canada, last month.

Wiberg, who had also taken second place in the second super-G held in Vail, Colorado, behind unherladed Russian Svetlana Gladishiva, had to be content with ninth place this time on a course which did not suit her.
"It was far too fast. It was more like a downhill," she said.
The race was marred by an accident in which French front runner Jenny Vallier lost balance on a bump just before the finish line and crashed into three photographers.
She was taken to hospital with a lung injury but it was not immediatly clear how serious it was, according to medical sources.
One of the photographers broke a leg in the accident which delayed the start of the race for half an hour.
It was the fifth consecutive victory by a German in the French resort since Seizinger won the three races held here last year while Martina Ertl won a giant slalom two years ago.
Ertl took fifth spot this time, confirming the Germans would be hard to beat this season.
Austrian Renate Goetschl, winner of the second downhill of the season in Vail, took fourth place. She looks like being the main threat to the Germans this winter.
Local fans also had reason to celebrate as three Frenchwomen finished among the top 10 -- Florence Masnada was sixth, Carole Montillet seventh and Laetitia Dalloz 10th.

The Germans will again be among the ones to watch in the giant slalom here on Friday. Italian Sabina Panzanini won the inaugural giant slalom of the season in Park City, Utah, last month ahead of Austria's Anita Wachter and Seizinger.
